extracted.intended_audience: media organizations, journalists, dpa customers, and the interested public
extracted.subtask_description: Editorial and organizational standards of a major news agency (dpa) describing principles for producing and disseminating news: factual verification, independence, impartiality, reliability, governance, use of AI, and audience relevance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Den Fakten verpflichtet (Committed to the facts)
rubrics_metrics.description: "Den Fakten verpflichtet" — the agency states that an enlightened democratic society needs verified information to make good, fact-based decisions and that an independent news agency is necessary for that.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasizes the normative role of verified information for democracy: reporting should be factual and verified because this underpins public decision-making. Use this principle to judge whether content is evidence-based and serves public information needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unabhängigkeit (Independence)
rubrics_metrics.description: dpa's independence is guaranteed (founded 1949 as a cooperative; more than 170 shareholders guarantee independence). The agency receives no grants from state bodies, companies or private persons and is financed exclusively by its own business activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Content, funding, and governance must avoid undue external influence. Financial and ownership independence is presented as a core pillar supporting editorial independence; verify absence of external funding or sponsorship that could bias coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Überparteilichkeit (Nonpartisanship / Impartiality)
rubrics_metrics.description: The dpa reports strictly "überparteilich" — committed to facts but to no political direction, religion, culture, party, company or other group.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reporting should be neutral and not favor any political or interest group. Evaluate language, sourcing, and framing for signs of partisanship or alignment with particular actors; prefer balanced presentation of competing views.

rubrics_metrics.name: Zuverlässigkeit — Richtigkeit geht immer vor Geschwindigkeit (Reliability — accuracy before speed)
rubrics_metrics.description: "Richtigkeit geht immer vor Geschwindigkeit. Recherche und Überprüfen von Informationen sind das wesentliche Handwerkszeug der dpa."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize verification and fact-checking over publishing quickly. Methods should include careful research and checking of information; avoid publishing unverified claims even under time pressure. This is a core evaluative criterion for story readiness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Einsatz von KI (Use of AI — supportive only; human final decision)
rubrics_metrics.description: dpa uses AI applications (examples: graphic generators like FireFly, translation aids like DeepL, transcription tools like Happy Scribe, chatbots like ChatGPT) for products and services; AI tools are used only supportively and do not replace journalistic core competencies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: AI may assist (graphics, translations, transcripts, suggestions), but tasks that require checking, researching and evaluating must remain human responsibilities. Every piece of content produced with AI support must be reviewed and the final decision to publish must be made by a human. Cite examples of tools but maintain transparency about AI use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relevanz & Trend-Tracking (Audience relevance: tracking social media and public concerns)
rubrics_metrics.description: Questions to guide coverage: What trends on social media? What moves people? Which of that must enter our reporting? 'Tracking, Themen, Tempo' are described as the coordinates for dpa.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coverage should be guided by what is relevant to audiences — monitor social media and public conversation to decide which topics to include. Balance timeliness (tempo) with topicality (themen) and informed tracking. Use agile methods and empathy to maximize usefulness to customers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial leadership and oversight (Governance ensures standards)
rubrics_metrics.description: Editorial leadership: dpa is led by management and the editor-in-chief; the supervisory board is elected by the shareholders' assembly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clear editorial structures and supervisory mechanisms exist to uphold standards and independence. Organizational responsibility for final editorial decisions lies with designated human leaders (management/chefredaktion), which supports accountability and adherence to the agency's principles.
